observations: 13 actual executable/socket/filesystem tests;50 existing binary tests including shared HTTP server boundaries;3 CLI contract tests;zero skipped.
Login/logout use existing session routes; protected origin-bound credential file, nonblocking parent custody and no-overwrite synchronized publication.

Actual late destination creation preserves external bytes and issued staging. Concurrent login refuses before a second issuance; SIGTERM closes the socket, releases the lock and preserves unresolved staging.
A genuinely filled stdout pipe yields exit1 with the issued file retained. This proves bounded termination for that sink, not general filesystem syscall deadlines or power-loss durability.
Held partial response reaches the six-second total deadline and the independent peer observes EOF. Redirect target receives no connection.

Job pages preserve signed64/unsigned64 extremes and zero checkpoint; reject inconsistent order, repeated IDs, overflow, unknown/duplicate/missing fields. Exact128KiB succeeds; one extra byte, chunked overflow, truncation and33headers refuse without page output.
Private files with unsafe modes, hard links, symlinks, extra fields, wrong formats or excessive bytes refuse without network.
regressions: Initial login tests failed because the command was absent; first implementation passed. Jobs first failed for missing command then passed.
